item.title: Local roundup: Schinkelshoek wins two OFSAA golds; GOHL expands; Ohta re-signs
item.description: Pain Court’s Gavin Schinkelshoek won two gold medals at the OFSAA swimming championship this week in Windsor.

item.title: Pain Court's Pat Myers refereeing hockey at Paralympics
item.description: Pat Myers isn’t vying for a medal at the Milano Cortina Games, but he expects the experience to be worth its weight in gold.

item.title: Woman charged in Blenheim multi-unit fire receives bail
item.description: A Blenheim woman charged with arson after a fire displaced residents of a multi-unit residential building earlier this year will be released on bail. Jocelyne Charuk, 42, appeared in person in the Ontario Court of Justice in Chatham on Friday. item.title: Ursuline wrestlers win three OFSAA medals
item.description: The Ursuline Lancers collected a school record three medals at the OFSAA wrestling championship this week in Peterborough.

item.title: LTVCA keeping an eye on watershed after heavy rain
item.description: Warm weather and heavy rain have conservation authority officials monitoring the Thames River watershed. The watershed received 10-20 mm of rain on Thursday, which was followed up Friday night by an additional 10-20 mm as thunderstorms passed through, said the Lower Thames Valley Conservation Authority. item.title: Purple bench recognizes victims of intimate partner violence, trafficking
item.description: A purple bench unveiled in Zonta Park in Chatham on Friday will serve to support and honour victims of domestic violence, sexual assault and human trafficking.
